I read the draft. Honestly, it feels heavy. Everything is must this, must that.
Only three lines are must. Everything else is should or may. Which one felt heavy to you?
The training. Can we say managers should complete it, and see who does?
We can write should. But then, if something happens in a team, the company has no answer for why the manager was never trained.
And the workload paragraph? That one is a should, and it is the one I actually care about.

Then it has to change. If it is part of the duty of care, should is too weak. And in the same document there is the opposite problem: we wrote that employees must report a concern. Nobody can be obliged to report. That one has to become may.
So you are making one line stronger and one line weaker, in the same review.
Exactly. The strength of the verb has to match the strength of the obligation. Anything else is a promise the company cannot keep.
Every manager must complete the training this quarter.
A written grievance has to be answered within five working days.
You should document the conversation afterwards.
Nobody may investigate a complaint about their own team.
The strength of the verb has to match the strength of the obligation.

Good afternoon. I am the compliance officer for the region, and I have ten minutes, so I will be direct. Three things are obligations, not recommendations. First, every manager must complete the psychosocial risk training before the end of the quarter. There is no exception for people who joined this year. Second, any grievance received in writing has to be answered in writing within five working days. Not a phone call. In writing. Third, nobody may investigate a complaint about their own team. If the complaint is about your area, it goes to me. Everything else in the document is guidance: you should document the conversation, and you should tell the employee what happens next, but nobody will discipline you for the format you use.

Hi Adriana, it is Paula from the legal team. I read the draft of the wellbeing policy and there is one thing you need to change before it goes out. In the section about workload, you wrote that managers should review the distribution of tasks every quarter. If that is what the duty of care requires, it cannot be should. It has to be must, or a lawyer will read it as optional in the first hearing we have. And the opposite is also true: in the paragraph about the anonymous channel, you wrote that employees must report any concern. Nobody can be obliged to report. That one has to become may. One word in each paragraph. Call me if you want to go through it together.
